# Migration: v2.8 → v2.9

## Summary

v2.9 changes who owns your templates. Until now every migration copied the
scaffold's templates over yours, so tailoring one meant losing the edit at the
next upgrade. From v2.9 the templates are **seeded**: the scaffold installs a
working default, `docs/.pdocs-seed.json` records what it installed, and a later
migration updates a template only while you have not touched it — reporting it,
rather than overwriting it, once you have.

It also opens the document-type vocabulary. A project can declare its own folder
(`docs/runbooks/` carrying `type: runbook`) in `.project-docs.json` and the lint
accepts it.

Nothing you have written changes. This migration adds a file, refreshes the CLI
and `docs/SCHEMA.md`, and leaves the content of every template as it is.

**Three words this guide uses throughout**, defined fully in the
`docs/SCHEMA.md` you install at step 5, under "Who owns which file":

- **owned** — the scaffold overwrites it on every migration. It is read by code,
  so your copy has to match. `scripts/pdocs/` and `docs/SCHEMA.md` are owned.
- **seeded** — installed once, then negotiated by hash. The templates.
- **theirs** — never touched. `.project-docs.json`, your documents,
  `docs/index.md`.

## What's New

- **`docs/.pdocs-seed.json`** — the seed manifest. Docs-root-relative path →
  sha256 of the bytes the scaffold installed.
- **`scripts/pdocs/seed.ts`** — reads it back and decides, per file: `update`,
  `install`, `keep-modified`, `keep-unknown`, `keep-deleted`. **Nothing calls it
  yet**; it is the API the next migration uses. The record has to exist before
  there is anything to reconcile against.
- **`lint.types` in `.project-docs.json`** — declare your own folders and the
  `type` their pages carry.
- **`pdocs find --type` now refuses an unknown type**, naming the set it knows.
  It used to return `count: 0` at exit 0, which reads as "nothing matches".
- **A "Who owns which file" section in `docs/SCHEMA.md`.**

## What Moved

Nothing.

## What's Removed

Nothing.

## Before you start

**Run every command from the project root** — the directory holding
`.project-docs.json`. Every path below is relative to it.

**Shell variables do not survive between steps.** If you are an agent running
each block as a separate shell invocation, `$SCAFFOLD` and `$SKILL_DIR` are
empty in the next block. They are written as variables for readability; the
reliable approach is to resolve each once and **paste the literal path** into
the steps that use it. Every step that depends on one checks it first, and those
checks exit non-zero.

## Step-by-Step Migration

### [Agent] 1. Commit or stash your work first

```bash
git status --short
```

Expected: no output. If there is any, commit or stash before continuing — this
migration rewrites `docs/SCHEMA.md` and `scripts/pdocs/`, and a dirty tree makes
its changes indistinguishable from yours.

### [Agent] 2. Confirm the tools this guide needs

```bash
for t in bun cookiecutter git npx; do
  command -v "$t" >/dev/null || { echo "MISSING: $t"; missing=1; }
done
[ -z "$missing" ] || { echo "STOP — install the tools listed above"; exit 1; }
echo "tools ok"
```

All four are used: `cookiecutter` and `git` in step 3 (the `gh:` prefix clones
over the network), `bun` from step 6, `npx` in step 7. The loop reports
**every** missing tool rather than stopping at the first.

### [Agent] 3. Generate the current scaffold locally

The scaffold is generated into a throwaway directory so later steps have a
pristine copy to copy **from**. It is not an install.

```bash
rm -rf .scaffold-tmp
cookiecutter gh:ichabodcole/project-docs-scaffold-template --no-input \
  -o .scaffold-tmp install_target="New project folder"
SCAFFOLD=$(ls -d .scaffold-tmp/*/ | head -1)
echo "scaffold at: $SCAFFOLD"
```

`rm -rf .scaffold-tmp` is not optional. Without it a leftover directory from an
interrupted run makes `cookiecutter` fail while `ls -d` still finds the
**stale** copy — and every later step then copies from the wrong version,
silently.

Verify this is the **project root** of the scaffold, not its `docs/`:

```bash
[ -n "$SCAFFOLD" ] && [ -f "$SCAFFOLD/docs/SCHEMA.md" ] && [ -d "$SCAFFOLD/scripts/pdocs" ] \
  || { echo "STOP — SCAFFOLD is wrong or unset: '$SCAFFOLD'"; exit 1; }
echo "SCAFFOLD ok: $SCAFFOLD"
```

Note the literal path it echoes. You will need it again in steps 4, 5 and 9.

### [Agent] 4. Refresh the CLI

`scripts/pdocs/` is **owned** — delivered, not handed over.

```bash
[ -d "$SCAFFOLD/scripts/pdocs" ] || { echo "STOP — re-derive SCAFFOLD (step 3)"; exit 1; }
cp -R "$SCAFFOLD/scripts/pdocs/." scripts/pdocs/
```

`cp -R src/. dest/` **merges**: it refreshes and adds, and never deletes a file
in `dest` that is absent from `src`. Nothing was removed from the CLI this
round, so a merge is sufficient here. A future migration that removes a file has
to delete it explicitly.

```bash
[ -f scripts/pdocs/seed.ts ] || { echo "STOP — seed.ts did not arrive"; exit 1; }
echo "seed.ts installed"
```

### [Agent] 5. Refresh `docs/SCHEMA.md`

Also **owned**: the lint implements it, so your copy has to match. Read its new
"Who owns which file" section once it lands — it is the contract the rest of
this guide assumes.

```bash
[ -f "$SCAFFOLD/docs/SCHEMA.md" ] || { echo "STOP — re-derive SCAFFOLD (step 3)"; exit 1; }
cp "$SCAFFOLD/docs/SCHEMA.md" docs/SCHEMA.md

grep -q 'Who owns which file' docs/SCHEMA.md || { echo "STOP — ownership section missing"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'Declaring your own folder' docs/SCHEMA.md || { echo "STOP — types section missing"; exit 1; }
echo "SCHEMA.md refreshed"
```

### [Agent] 6. Run the formatter — BEFORE recording hashes

```bash
npx prettier --write "docs/**/*.md"
```

Skip this **only** if your project does not use Prettier.

**Order matters here and it is the one thing in this guide that silently
destroys the migration if you get it wrong.** Step 7 records the sha256 of every
template's bytes. Formatting a template after that leaves it not matching its
own recorded hash, so the next migration reads it as edited by you and never
updates it again — the whole mechanism, opted out of, for files you never
touched. Format first, then record.

### [Agent] 7. Adopt your templates

This is the step the migration exists for. It records the sha256 of the
templates **already in your project** — not the scaffold's copies — so whatever
you have becomes the baseline.

`SKILL_DIR` is the `update-project-docs` skill directory. An agent that loaded
this skill has it as the "Base directory for this skill"; otherwise it is the
directory two levels above this file. Set it literally:

```bash
SKILL_DIR="<the update-project-docs skill directory>"
[ -f "${SKILL_DIR}/migrations/scripts/migrate-v2.8-to-v2.9.ts" ] \
  || { echo "STOP — set SKILL_DIR to the skill directory (got '${SKILL_DIR}')"; exit 1; }
echo "SKILL_DIR ok"
```

Look before you write. `--dry-run` lists every template it would record and
changes nothing:

```bash
bun "${SKILL_DIR}/migrations/scripts/migrate-v2.8-to-v2.9.ts" --dry-run
```

**Read the list.** It should name the templates you recognise — one per category
folder, plus the ones under `docs/projects/TEMPLATES/`. A count of `0`, or a
list naming files you do not recognise, means you are in the wrong directory or
your `docsRoot` is not what you think; stop and work out which before writing.

Then run it:

```bash
bun "${SKILL_DIR}/migrations/scripts/migrate-v2.8-to-v2.9.ts"
```

Verify — the count must be **non-zero**, because a manifest recording nothing is
written, valid, and useless:

```bash
[ -f docs/.pdocs-seed.json ] || { echo "STOP — no manifest written"; exit 1; }
RECORDED=$(grep -c '": "' docs/.pdocs-seed.json)
[ "$RECORDED" -gt 0 ] || { echo "STOP — manifest recorded 0 templates"; exit 1; }
echo "manifest written, $RECORDED entries"
```

Commit `docs/.pdocs-seed.json`, and make sure it is not caught by `.gitignore` —
a manifest that never reaches the repository cannot be read by the next
migration.

**What this step does not do.** It compares nothing and replaces nothing. On
this run nothing is known — your project has no record of what the scaffold once
installed — so every template is adopted as it stands. A template you edited
three versions ago is recorded as though it had shipped that way. That is the
honest answer, and it is why this is a one-time adoption rather than a
reconciliation. From the next migration on, the comparison runs.

### [Agent] 8. Verify the tree against the CLI

```bash
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check
echo "check exit: $?"
```

Expected: `docs-lint: clean`, exit 0.

If it is not clean, the CLI you installed in step 4 is newer than the one your
tree was written against — read the reported problems, which name the file and
the rule. Nothing in this migration changes a document, so any failure is a
pre-existing gap the newer lint now sees.

Then confirm the new refusal works:

```bash
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts find --type nosuchtype; echo "exit: $?"
```

Expected: a rejection naming the types it knows, **exit 2** — not an empty
result at exit 0.

### [Agent] 9. Update the version markers and clean up

Both markers carry the scaffold release you migrated TO.

```bash
[ -f "$SCAFFOLD/docs/README.md" ] || { echo "STOP — re-derive SCAFFOLD (step 3)"; exit 1; }
VERSION=$(grep -m1 docs_version "$SCAFFOLD/docs/README.md" | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')

case "$VERSION" in
  [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) echo "migrating to $VERSION" ;;
  *) echo "STOP — VERSION is '$VERSION', not a version number"; exit 1 ;;
esac
```

**Do not skip that check.** With `$SCAFFOLD` empty the `grep` fails, `VERSION`
becomes the empty string, and the two `sed` calls below write `docs_version: ""`
and `"version": ""` — at exit 0, into both markers, where they then agree with
each other and pass every check that only compares them.

```bash
sed -i.bak -E "s/^docs_version: \".*\"/docs_version: \"$VERSION\"/" docs/README.md && rm docs/README.md.bak
sed -i.bak -E "s/^([[:space:]]*\"version\": )\"[^\"]*\"/\1\"$VERSION\"/" .project-docs.json && rm .project-docs.json.bak
```

The second expression is anchored with `^`. Unanchored it rewrites **every**
line holding a `"version":` pair, including any nested key of your own — and
`.project-docs.json` is **theirs**, so a migration must not touch anything in it
beyond the marker.

Confirm they hold the version you expected — not merely that they match each
other — then remove the scaffold:

```bash
grep docs_version docs/README.md
grep '"version"' .project-docs.json
rm -rf .scaffold-tmp
```

## Cross-Reference Updates

None. No path changed and no document type was added or removed.

## Optional: declare your own document type

Not part of the migration — do it whenever you want one. To add `docs/runbooks/`
carrying `type: runbook`, add the folder to a tier array and name its type:

```jsonc
// .project-docs.json — "lint" block, existing entries omitted for brevity
"workbench": ["backlog", "briefs", "runbooks"],
"types": { "runbooks": "runbook" }
```

The tier follows from the array the folder is listed in: `workbench` for the
thin checks, `durable` for the full graph tier including catalog reachability. A
declared type is lintable but not creatable — `pdocs new` ships no template for
it and says so. `docs/SCHEMA.md` has the detail.

## Verification

- [ ] `git status --short` was clean before starting
- [ ] `scripts/pdocs/seed.ts` exists
- [ ] `docs/SCHEMA.md` contains "Who owns which file"
- [ ] Prettier ran **before** the manifest was written
- [ ] `docs/.pdocs-seed.json` exists, lists a non-zero number of templates, and
      is committed (not gitignored)
- [ ] Every recorded hash matches its file — confirm with:
      `bun -e 'const{loadManifest,verdictFor}=await import("./scripts/pdocs/seed.ts");const m=loadManifest("docs");const bad=Object.keys(m.files).filter(k=>verdictFor(m,"docs",k)!=="update");console.log(bad.length?"STALE: "+bad.join(", "):"all hashes match")'`
- [ ] `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check` exits 0
- [ ] `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts find --type nosuchtype` exits 2
- [ ] `docs_version` and `.project-docs.json` both hold the version you expected
- [ ] `.scaffold-tmp/` removed
- [ ] The migration's changes are committed
